title: Read a bǎ sentence as what happened to it
summary: When the marker ba appears, look for the known object first and the outcome at the end.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: A 把 bǎ sentence is easy to misread if you treat 把 bǎ as a verb every time. Ask one question when you see it: what was done to the thing already in mind? The object between 把 bǎ and the verb is something both speakers can identify, and the verb cannot be left bare; something at the end must close the deal, usually 了 le, a result, or a direction. So 请把门关上 qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng (please close the door) is a complete instruction and 请把门 qǐng bǎ mén is not a sentence. Read these in order, object first, outcome last, and the meaning arrives in the right shape.
